hook: A new electric motor design just hit 30,000 rpm, changing everything.

sections.voiceover: A new electric motor design just hit 30,000 rpm, changing everything.
sections.visual_cue: Macro shot of a high-speed electric motor spinning rapidly in a lab.
sections.sfx_cue: High-pitched electric whine increasing in frequency.
b_roll: ZF High Revolution Drive laboratory test bench

sections.voiceover: Engineers in Friedrichshafen developed the High Revolution Drive, a 3-in-1 unit combining a motor, power electronics, and gear transmission. How much smaller and lighter is this Friedrichshafen-engineered High Revolution Drive?
sections.visual_cue: 3D exploded view of the ZF High Revolution Drive unit showing internal components.
sections.sfx_cue: Mechanical clicking as parts assemble in the animation.
b_roll: Technical diagram of a 3-in-1 electric drive unit

sections.voiceover: But ZF also cuts magnet mass by 50 percent, raising the stakes for future efficiency.
sections.visual_cue: Comparison graphic showing a large magnet block shrinking to half its size.
b_roll: Close-up of rare-earth magnets on a manufacturing line

sections.voiceover: The High Revolution Drive is 25 percent smaller and lighter than an 18,000 rpm SELECT drive. This Friedrichshafen-based design uses 50 percent less magnet mass than the 18,000 rpm SELECT drive.
sections.visual_cue: Side-by-side scale comparison of the new drive against the older SELECT model.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft electronic chime indicating a successful measurement.

sections.voiceover: It spins at 30,000 rpm, redefining electric vehicle power density.
sections.visual_cue: Final close-up shot of the motor casing with the ZF logo visible.
b_roll: ZF High Revolution Drive unit on display
